title: CCIU opens a 15-classroom special education campus in Malvern
summary: The Chester County Intermediate Unit cut the ribbon Oct. 21 on its Child and Career Development Center Great Valley Campus at 40 Moores Rd., which houses four special education programs serving students from 31 school districts. The agency says the site took more than two years of planning and shortens travel for many families.

title: WCU marks 100 years of jazz with a three-day celebration Nov. 6-8
summary: West Chester University is honoring its Criterions Jazz Ensemble, rooted in the 1920s, with a free welcome concert Friday, Nov. 6, a free masterclass with vibraphonist Stefon Harris, a $100 dance soiree Saturday and a ticketed anniversary concert Sunday featuring new works by Bob Mintzer and Orrin Evans. The university is also raising money for a permanent jazz endowment.

title: West Pikeland calls an Oct. 26 special meeting to rethink the SALT building sale
summary: A week after voting 3-2 to put the township-owned cultural center at 1645 Art School Rd. up for sale, supervisors will meet again Monday, Oct. 26 at 7 p.m. to discuss options for the property. SALT Performing Arts, which has put about $400,000 into the building, holds a license that a buyer could end on 30 days' notice.

title: A readers' retreat built around West Chester's bookstores is set for Nov. 20-22
summary: Novelist JB Harris is bringing the first Future Famous Authors Bookish Retreat to the borough, with visits to Baldwin's Book Barn, Bookmarks and Leaves and Lore, an author panel dinner and rooms at the Book House Hotel and Hotel Indigo. It is aimed at readers, not aspiring writers.

title: Chester County Hospital opens an outpatient lactation center
summary: Penn Medicine Chester County Hospital has opened a center where new parents can book one-on-one sessions with lactation consultants after they go home with their baby.

title: Christmas Parade recruits 30 first-time walking marshals for Dec. 4
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce wants about 30 volunteers to walk alongside floats and bands and help judge entries at the Dec. 4 parade, which follows the 6:30 p.m. courthouse tree lighting. Marshals get a red hat and a yellow vest, and sign-ups run through the Chamber's parade page.

title: West Chester Refillery Station opens on East Street Road
summary: A refill shop selling household staples in bulk for customers' own containers has opened at 54 E. Street Rd., per the Inquirer's Chester County roundup.

title: Turks Head Wines adds a restaurant to its West Chester tasting room
summary: The California-focused winery at 120 N. Church St. began serving food this month and brought on chef Dave McDonald, formerly of Helm BYOB.

title: Pinckney Hill Commons unveils 70 feet of resident-painted murals
summary: Downingtown artist Adrian Martinez spent two years working with dozens of residents, many of them children, on three indoor murals of Albert Einstein, Benicio Del Toro and Cynthia Erivo at the 51-unit affordable housing complex. Mayor Lillian DeBaptiste gave Martinez a Key to the Borough at the unveiling.

title: West Chester's Centinel Spine files for a $100 million IPO
summary: The maker of prodisc cervical and lumbar disc replacement implants plans to list on the NYSE as CNTL, with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs leading the offering. It reported $85.2 million in revenue for the first half of 2026, up 42% from a year earlier.
